issues.description: The solution repository's PersonResource constructor takes a String parameter rather than a PersonService. The class declares a field of type PersonService and all REST endpoints call methods on this service, so the incorrect constructor parameter type causes a compile error and contradicts the intended dependency injection shown in the template and described in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java of the solution repository to accept a PersonService (e.g., public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }) so it matches the template, enables proper dependency injection, and compiles correctly.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect PersonResource to be constructed with a PersonService dependency (conceptual entity: PersonService). In the solution implementation, the PersonResource constructor declares a parameter of type String named personService instead of PersonService. This presents the same conceptual dependency with a different type identifier across artifacts, which breaks the expected mapping between the problem description, the template (which injects PersonService), and the solution. Students comparing artifacts will be confused about how the PersonService dependency is provided and wired into PersonResource.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution repository, change the PersonResource constructor parameter type from String to PersonService to match the conceptual dependency. Example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }
